subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Priya Shah <p.shah@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps (Acme)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and immediate next steps from our demo + the initial model shortlist for your use case (customer support summarization + intent routing).

Recap (quick):
- Demo covered Redwood inference runtime, live latency dashboards, and how we do KV-prefix caching for session-heavy flows.
- You confirmed goals: high accuracy on multi-turn summarization, <150ms token latency for interactive routing, and predictable unit cost for 10M monthly tokens.

Initial model shortlist (recommendations + tradeoffs):
1) Llama-2-13b-chat (q4_0 quant) — Best balance of accuracy and cost. Expected P50 token latency ~90ms on our 1xA100-equivalent profile, solid summary coherence. Good for early rollout.
2) Mistral-7b-instruct (q4) — Lowest cost and fastest latency (P50 ~45ms). Slightly more prompt engineering required; good option for high-throughput routing where cost is primary.
3) Redwood-30b-fp16 (serving profile) — Highest quality on edge cases and fewer hallucinations in our evals; higher cost and latency (P50 ~220ms) but strong for escalations/long-form summaries.

Why these three: they span cost/latency/quality tradeoffs and all have a compatible footprint for Redwood Dedicated or Hosted. We ran an internal eval on your seed prompt set (see attached) and included link to the full benchmark.

Attachments: acme-model-shortlist.csv (compact matrix), acme-prompt-set.md (seed prompts we used), benchmark-results-2026-02-25.pdf (detailed numbers). Also sharing the public eval URL: https://results.redwood.ai/reports/acme-eval-2026-02-25

Suggested next steps:
- You: confirm which two models you want a short pilot for (we recommend Llama-2-13b-chat + Mistral-7b).
- We (Redwood): provision trial endpoints and run your full prompt set (30k tokens) through both; deliver a comparison report with P50/P95 latency, token cost, and a small quality rubric (precision/recall on intent detect + summary ROUGE-ish score).
- Optional: we can run a focused hallucination/regression evaluation against your internal golden set if you can share a redacted sample.

Open questions I had from the call:
- Do you have a strict P95 latency SLO for the routing path? You mentioned <200ms earlier but I wanted to confirm.
- Any regulatory constraints on model outputs or data retention we should account for in the pilot (e.g., PII redaction rules)?

I’ll loop in Aditya to share the benchmark summary and cost math. Happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up next week to lock the pilot scope.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps (Acme)

Thanks Marissa — useful writeup. A few clarifying questions before we pick pilots:

1) P95 latency SLO: For the routing decision path (short prompts, <200 tokens), our internal target is P95 <= 150ms. Can you confirm which of the shortlisted models meet that on your hosted profile?

2) Hallucinations: we observed in the demo some odd generated action suggestions (e.g., suggesting incorrect product IDs). Do you have specific hallucination/regression numbers for the three models on the seed prompts?

3) Security: we will need the pilot to be within our VPC & logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that feasible for a short trial?

Finally — can you also include the prompt variations you tested? We want to understand sensitivity to system prompt changes.

If we can get P95 data and the hallucination numbers, we can lock the two pilots (we'd prefer cost + one higher-quality model).

Appreciate it,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Platform Engineering Lead | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acmecorp.com

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model shortlist & next steps (Acme)

Hi Alex — quick answers and numbers from our internal runs against the provided seed prompts (attached summary + full report link).

TL;DR
- Models meeting P95 <=150ms on our standard hosted profile: Mistral-7b-instruct (q4) ✓, Llama-2-13b-chat (q4_0) — borderline (P95 ~160-170ms depending on burst), Redwood-30b-fp16 ✗ (P95 ~320ms).
- Hallucination/regression: we ran a subset of 200 labeled examples (intent labels + ground-truth summaries). False action suggestions (hallucinated product IDs) rate: Mistral-7b: 6.2%, Llama-2-13b-chat: 3.8%, Redwood-30b-fp16: 1.4%.
- Cost estimates (approx tokens USD per 1M tokens on hosted): Mistral-7b-instruct ~ $280, Llama-2-13b-chat ~ $520, Redwood-30b-fp16 ~ $1,800. These assume our standard batching and prefix cache behavior for your traffic shape.

Notes and caveats:
- Llama-2-13b hits the P95 slightly above your 150ms target in our baseline; we can tune batching and prioritize routing profile which typically brings P95 below 150ms at modest cost (~5-10% more CPU/GPU priority). If P95 is a hard constraint, we recommend Mistral-7b for the routing path and Llama-2-13b for the escalation/summarization path.
- The hallucination numbers use Acme seed prompts (attached). If you share a private golden set, we can run a full regression check.
- VPC trial: we can provision a short-term private endpoint inside your VPC for the pilot (we've done similar for other accounts). Logs can be forwarded via syslog or a Splunk/Datadog sink. Need a quick networking contact to set up peering/policies.

Attachments included: benchmark-results-2026-02-25.pdf (full metrics), acme-prompt-set.md (prompts & prompt variants), acme-model-shortlist.csv (cost/latency matrix).

Proposed pilot configuration:
- Pilot A (routing): Mistral-7b-instruct (q4) — 2 weeks, run entire 30k prompt set, measure P50/P95, token cost, operate inside VPC.
- Pilot B (summarization/escalation): Llama-2-13b-chat (q4_0) — 2 weeks, run selected high-difficulty prompts, collect quality/regression metrics.

If that aligns, Marissa / Dev can start provisioning.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Alex — great, thanks for the clarifying Qs. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) Pilot selection: you mentioned cost + one higher-quality model — based on Aditya's numbers, that would be Mistral-7b-instruct (routing) + Llama-2-13b-chat (escalation). Please confirm by EOD today and we'll spin up endpoints.

2) VPC trial: Dev will reach out to your infra contact to schedule a 30-min networking window (peering + logs). Dev — can you send the network checklist?

3) Evaluation: once endpoints are live we'll run the full 30k prompt set and deliver a comparison report within 5 business days. We'll include P50/P95, token cost, hallucination/regression rates, and a short recommended mitigation plan (prompt tweaks + confidence-threshold routing).

4) Follow-up call: propose Wed 3/4 9:00am PT to review results. Calendar invite to follow if that works.

I've attached the shortlist CSV and prompt set again. If you can also share a redacted golden set for hallucination checks, that will speed the regression analysis.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a short pilot so you can validate the tradeoffs in your environment.
